tasks.description: Extract and curate the SKEMPI-v2 mutation cohort. Parse skempi_v2.csv fields: PDB id, Mutation (chain-annotated, e.g., 'BN501Y'), ddG, Temperature (K), Method, Reference, protein labels. Filter: (a) direct SARS-CoV-2 RBD-ACE2 entries (PDB 6M0J, 6LZG, 7C8D, 6VW1 where present); (b) fallback cohort = all protein-protein interface mutations with reported ddG and T in [277-311 K] to power cross-complex statistics. Normalize all ddG to kcal/mol (convert kJ/mol entries), deduplicate, record N per complex. Output tidy CSV: pdb_id, chain, wt_aa, position, mut_aa, ddG_kcal, T_K, method, reference.
tasks.expected_output: Tidy cohort CSV (>=50 interface mutations or documented cohort exhaustion), unit-normalized ddG in kcal/mol, temperature metadata, and cohort summary (N, ddG range, T distribution).

tasks.description: Build the N501Y validation anchor from literature. Retrieve published SPR/BLI measurements of RBD-ACE2 affinity change for N501Y (expected stabilization ddG ~ +0.5 to +1.0 kcal/mol; sources: Lan et al. 2020, Starr et al. 2020 deep mutational scanning, Wang et al.) and extract DMS-derived ddG distribution for position 501. doc_reader_agent reads full texts; fact_checker_agent verifies every numerical KD/ddG claim against sources; summarizer_agent condenses into a benchmark table (source, method, KD_wt, KD_N501Y, ddG, T).
tasks.expected_output: Benchmark table with >=3 independent N501Y ddG estimates (with uncertainties and temperatures) plus DMS ddG distribution for residue 501.

tasks.description: Compute interface structural features for the RBD-ACE2 complex. Download PDB 6M0J (primary) and 6LZG (replicate) via code_executor (Biopython/requests). For every cohort mutation position (including residue 501 on both partners), compute: buried SASA (FreeSASA/NACCESS), H-bond count (heavy-atom distance <= 3.5 A, DHA angle >= 120 deg), salt bridges, contact density (heavy-atom pairs <= 4.5 A), and aromatic stacking potential (ring centroid distance <= 6 A) to test the N501Y pi-pi/shape-complementarity hypothesis. Output a feature matrix keyed by (pdb_id, chain, position).
tasks.expected_output: Feature matrix CSV: per-position bSASA, H-bond count, salt bridges, contact density, and aromatic-stacking score for every cohort mutation site.

tasks.description: Run computational ddG predictions on the curated cohort using two orthogonal methods: (1) FoldX 5 BuildModel (repairPDB then BuildModel, 5 runs/mutation, pH 7, ionic strength 0.05 M, T 298 K); (2) Rosetta ddG (cartesian_ddg / interface ddG, ref2015 soft-repulsive score, 3 relax rounds). Structures: 6M0J primary, 6LZG replicate. Apply N501Y and all cohort mutations in silico; record per-method ddG and inter-method agreement (Pearson rho).
tasks.expected_output: Table of experimental vs FoldX vs Rosetta ddG per mutation, with per-method RMSE vs experiment and inter-method correlation coefficient.

tasks.description: Statistical analysis of thermodynamic determinants. (a) Spearman and Pearson correlations between experimental ddG and each structural feature (bSASA, H-bonds, salt bridges, contact density, aromatic score) with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR < 0.05; (b) multiple linear regression ddG ~ features with 1000-sample bootstrap 95% CIs and 80/20 train/test split (report held-out R^2 and RMSE); (c) permutation null (1000 shuffles of ddG) for empirical p-values. Implemented in code_executor (pandas/scipy/statsmodels/sklearn).
tasks.expected_output: Correlation table with FDR-corrected p-values, regression coefficients with bootstrap CIs, held-out R^2 and RMSE, and permutation null distribution.

tasks.description: Enthalpy/entropy decomposition. (a) Where SKEMPI-v2 provides multiple measurement temperatures for homologous interface mutations, perform van 't Hoff analysis (ln KD vs 1/T) to estimate dH and dS; (b) otherwise use FoldX energy-component decomposition (van der Waals, electrostatics, solvation, H-bond terms) on N501Y and cohort mutations to attribute affinity change to enthalpic (electrostatics/H-bonds) vs entropic/packing (solvation/vdW) contributions; (c) quantify the fraction of N501Y ddG explained by aromatic-packing (vdW) vs H-bond-loss terms.
tasks.expected_output: Decomposition table: per-mutation ddG split into energy components; van 't Hoff dH/dS estimates where temperature series exist; N501Y attribution summary (vdW vs electrostatics vs H-bond fractions).

tasks.description: Pre-registered falsification test. H1: local interface structural features (esp. buried SASA and aromatic-packing potential) predict experimental ddG. Criteria: (F1) best regression held-out RMSE < 1.0 kcal/mol AND Spearman rho >= 0.3 with FDR p < 0.05; (F2) FoldX/Rosetta ddG RMSE vs experiment < 1.0 kcal/mol; (F3) predicted N501Y ddG within +/-0.5 kcal/mol of the literature benchmark (+0.5 to +1.0 kcal/mol stabilization); (F4) permutation null p < 0.05 for the top-ranked feature. Verdict rule: failure of >= 2 of F1-F4 falsifies the structural-determinants hypothesis in favor of the null (affinity change not predictable from local interface features). fact_checker_agent verifies all reported statistics.
tasks.expected_output: Falsification scorecard with computed statistics and pass/fail per criterion F1-F4, plus an explicit supported/falsified verdict.

tasks.description: Generate the discovery report: (i) cohort definition and data provenance; (ii) determinant ranking from regression with bootstrap CIs; (iii) N501Y mechanistic attribution (aromatic packing/vdW vs H-bond loss); (iv) model performance against pre-registered thresholds F1-F4; (v) explicit falsification verdict and limitations (single-mutation scope, SKEMPI cohort size, force-field error, temperature heterogeneity). All numerical claims verified by fact_checker_agent; evidence condensed by summarizer_agent.
tasks.expected_output: Structured discovery report containing the falsification scorecard, determinant ranking with uncertainty, N501Y ddG benchmark comparison, and a limitations section.

plan.rationale: Revision addresses all seven critique points. (1) Placeholders eliminated: Task rev_1_4 names concrete protocols (FoldX 5 BuildModel, pH 7, ionic 0.05 M; Rosetta ddG with ref2015) on explicit structures (PDB 6M0J primary, 6LZG replicate). (2) Statistics operationalized: rev_1_5 specifies Spearman/Pearson correlations with BH-FDR, multiple regression with 1000-sample bootstrap CIs, 80/20 train/test split, and permutation nulls. (3) Falsification pre-registered: rev_1_7 defines thresholds F1-F4 (held-out RMSE < 1.0 kcal/mol, Spearman rho >= 0.3, N501Y prediction within +/-0.5 kcal/mol of literature benchmark, permutation p < 0.05). (4) Scope fixed: rev_1_1 defines an explicit mutation cohort (RBD-ACE2 PDB entries 6M0J/6LZG/7C8D/6VW1 plus fallback interface-mutation cohort) instead of relying on the single N501Y point; rev_1_2 supplements with DMS data. (5) Thermodynamic decomposition added: rev_1_6 performs van 't Hoff analysis using SKEMPI temperature metadata plus FoldX energy-component attribution. (6) Boilerplate agent rules removed; structural tooling (PDB retrieval, FreeSASA, contact maps) assigned via code_executor/experiment_agent. (7) Validation anchor added: rev_1_2 benchmarks against published N501Y ddG (~+0.5 to +1.0 kcal/mol). Parallelism increased: rev_1_1, rev_1_2, rev_1_3 run concurrently with zero dependencies; rev_1_6 depends only on rev_1_1.

Extract wild-type and mutant Kd and recompute ddG = R*T*ln(Kd_mut/Kd_wt) at T=298.15 K (R=1.987 cal/mol/K), cross-checking against the dataset's reported ddG column. plan.rationale: Hypothesis: the N501Y substitution in the SARS-CoV-2 RBD receptor-binding motif enhances ACE2 binding affinity primarily through enthalpic gains - new aromatic contacts (possible pi-stacking/cation-pi) with ACE2 Tyr41, a tyrosyl hydroxyl hydrogen bond, and improved van der Waals packing near ACE2 Lys353/Asp38 - partially offset by entropic costs of side-chain rigidification. SKEMPI-v2 provides experimentally calibrated mutation effects (ddG = R*T*ln(Kd_mut/Kd_wt)) to quantify these determinants empirically. Because the 2019 SKEMPI-v2 release may predate SARS-CoV-2 structures, the plan includes an explicit contingency: calibrate on homologous CoV RBD-ACE2 mutations and supplement N501Y values from primary literature, with every number fact-checked. This is hypothesis-driven exploitation of a known empirical dataset: exploration_ratio is set to 0.3 as the design budget, realized as a single bounded exploratory acquisition task (task_1_1, is_exploration=true; 1/7 tasks, ~12% of estimated minutes) while all other tasks are typed analysis/verification/synthesis/audit. The dependency graph references actual task IDs and is schedulable with parallelism: after task_1_1, task_1_4 (doc_reader_agent) runs concurrently with the task_1_2→task_1_3 analysis chain; task_1_5 (fact_checker_agent) converges all branches into a claim ledger; task_1_6 (summarizer_agent) condenses only VERIFIED claims into the report; task_1_7 (fact_checker_agent) performs the pre-submission audit.

tasks.description: SHARED STRUCTURE PREPARATION (dependency for task_1_2 and task_1_4): Fetch 6M0J via pdb_fetcher. Build WT (N501) and mutant (Y501) RBD-ACE2 models once using pdbfixer at pH 7.4; minimize 500 steps with OpenMM (no MD trajectories). Save both prepared structures to a shared workspace path recorded in metadata. Verify mutant placement with a single-rotamer pass plus a 3-rotamer tyrosine scan (chi angles) saved as alternates for downstream tasks. fact_checker_agent confirms pdbfixer+OpenMM-only workflow is sufficient for SASA and rigid-receptor rescoring (pyrosetta optional; log fallback if pip install pyrosetta fails).
tasks.expected_output: Paths to minimized WT and Y501 structures (plus 3 Y501 rotamer alternates), preparation log, pyrosetta fallback status in metadata

tasks.description: FALSIFIER 1 (magnitude attack): Download SKEMPI-v2 (github.com/haddocking/skempi2 CSV) via code_executor. Filter entries with PDB 6M0J or 6LZG and RBD mutations at position 501. CONTINGENCY (declared): if the filter returns zero rows (likely — SKEMPI coverage of SARS-CoV-2 RBD-ACE2 point mutants at 501 is not guaranteed), fall back in order to (i) adjacent RBD-ACE2 SKEMPI mutations as a calibration set, and (ii) Starr et al. 2020 deep mutational scanning values (N501Y ΔΔG ≈ -0.5 to -1.6 kcal/mol across studies) as the primary empirical source; record which source was used in metadata. Compute ΔΔG_bind = RT ln(Kd_mut/Kd_wt) at reported temperature with scipy; bootstrap 10,000 resamples for 95% CI. THRESHOLD CALIBRATION GATE: before applying falsification thresholds, fact_checker_agent verifies both the Starr reference values and the SKEMPI-derived point estimates against the World Model, and must justify or widen the interval [-1.8, -1.4] relative to the literature range (-1.0 to -1.4); if the fact_checker cannot justify the narrow interval, the pre-registered interval is widened to [-1.8, -1.0] and the change is logged. MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE OUTCOMES (using the fact_checker-approved interval): (A) N501Y ΔΔG within approved interval → magnitude pillar SURVIVES; (B) ΔΔG outside approved interval → magnitude pillar FALSIFIED.
tasks.expected_output: Point estimate + 95% CI of N501Y ΔΔG (SKEMPI or declared fallback source), fact_checker-approved threshold interval with justification log, literature comparison table, verdict A or B

tasks.description: FALSIFIER 2 (mechanism attack — desolvation/entropy pillar): Using the shared prepared structures from task_1_0 (dependency), compute SASA of residue 501 in WT (N) and mutant (Y) models with FreeSASA via code_executor, across all 3 Y501 rotamer alternates; report per-rotamer and best-case buried aromatic surface. Compute buried nonpolar surface: SASA_N_exposed vs SASA_Y_exposed (total/polar/nonpolar decomposition). Test the linear-scaling claim: if ΔS_desolv > 0 and proportional to buried aromatic area, the hydrophobic contribution must be FAVORABLE. MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE OUTCOMES: (A) tyrosine buries ≥40 Å² additional nonpolar surface in at least one rotamer AND hydrophobic term is favorable with the polar OH compensated → mechanism pillar SURVIVES; (B) no rotamer buries ≥40 Å², or the polar OH group remains solvent-exposed/uncompensated in the best-burying rotamer → desolvation-entropy mechanism FALSIFIED as dominant term; enthalpic H-bond/polar arguments must dominate instead.
tasks.expected_output: Per-rotamer SASA decomposition table (total/polar/nonpolar for N501 vs Y501), buried area in Å², verdict A or B with structural rationale, pyrosetta fallback log inherited from task_1_0

tasks.description: FALSIFIER 3 (temperature-dependence pillar): Use pubmed_search and arxiv_search with queries: 'N501Y ACE2 binding thermodynamics temperature', 'SARS-CoV-2 RBD ACE2 van't Hoff enthalpy entropy', 'ACE2 spike binding ITC thermodynamic parameters'. Use doc_reader_agent on up to 3 full-text hits (e.g., Zhang et al. ITC studies of RBD-ACE2). Extract ΔH, ΔS, ΔCp for WT and N501Y RBD-ACE2 binding. fact_checker_agent verifies all extracted numerical values against the World Model. Test prediction: ΔΔG(T) = ΔΔH_0 - T·ΔS_desolv with ΔS_desolv > 0 implies d(ΔΔG)/dT > 0 (advantage weakens with T). MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE OUTCOMES: (A) literature ΔCp/ΔS data consistent with weakening advantage above 298 K → prediction SURVIVES; (B) literature shows ΔΔG is temperature-stable or strengthens with T, or binding is enthalpy-driven with ΔS < 0 → linear-in-T desolvation prediction FALSIFIED.
tasks.expected_output: Fact-checked thermodynamic parameter table (ΔH, TΔS, ΔCp for WT vs N501Y), extrapolated ΔΔG at 278/298/318 K, verdict A or B

tasks.description: FALSIFIER 4 (orthogonal computational attack — enthalpy vs entropy decomposition, SUGGESTIVE-strength claim): Using the shared prepared structures and rotamer alternates from task_1_0 (dependency), run Smina (or AutoDock Vina) rigid-receptor rescoring of WT N501 and each of the 3 Y501 rotamer models on ACE2 from 6M0J. Compute ΔΔG_vina (best rotamer). Separately compute per-residue contact counts (H-bonds via 3.5 Å / 120° cutoffs) for N501 and Y501 across rotamers. Contingency: if Smina/Vina installation fails, fact_checker_agent confirms fallback to OpenMM-based per-residue interaction energy scoring and the substitution is recorded. CLAIM DOWNGRADE per critique: Vina scores are not enthalpy/entropy decompositions; outcome (A) is classified as SUGGESTIVE evidence for an enthalpic/contact-driven mechanism, not mechanistic proof. MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE OUTCOMES: (A) Vina ΔΔG within ±0.5 kcal/mol of the empirical value AND a new Y501-mediated polar contact (e.g., Y501 OH to ACE2 Y41/T35 region) appears in ≥2 of 3 rotamers → SUGGESTIVE enthalpic/contact-driven mechanism, counted as a WEAKENING (not falsifying) vote against the desolvation-dominance claim; (B) Vina fails to reproduce ΔΔG (error > 1.5 kcal/mol) → inconclusive for mechanism but flags force-field inadequacy, feeding synthesis task; (C) intermediate error (0.5–1.5 kcal/mol) → no vote cast, logged for synthesis.
tasks.expected_output: ΔΔG_vina per Y501 rotamer, H-bond/contact inventory for both variants, verdict A, B, or C with suggestive/decisive classification, fallback log if docking binary unavailable

tasks.description: ADJUDICATION: Collect verdicts from task_1_1, task_1_2, task_1_3, and task_1_4. Use summarizer_agent to build an evidence matrix (pillar: magnitude / desolvation mechanism / T-dependence / enthalpic alternative; verdict per task, with task_1_4 weighted as suggestive). Decision rule: hypothesis is FALSIFIED if ≥2 of 3 core pillars (tasks 1_1, 1_2, 1_3) fail; WEAKENED if 1 core pillar fails OR task_1_4 returns suggestive outcome (A); SURVIVES only if all three core pillars hold and task_1_4 does not return (A). fact_checker_agent verifies every numerical claim in the matrix against the World Model. Produce a falsification report with explicit mutually-exclusive outcome statements. CONTINGENCY EXPLORATION BRANCH: if the overall status is SURVIVES, the report must include one exploratory next-cycle attack vector (ΔCp-based calorimetric test or small-scale alchemical FEP) formulated as a research question for cycle 2; if FALSIFIED/WEAKENED, recommend repair or replacement vectors instead.
tasks.expected_output: Structured falsification report: pillar-by-pillar verdicts, overall hypothesis status (FALSIFIED/WEAKENED/SURVIVES), verified numbers, next-cycle attack or exploration recommendations

plan.rationale: Revised SIEGE plan addressing all critique flaws: (1) research_objective populated; (2) exploration_ratio corrected to 0.0 (all tasks is_exploration=false, with exploration deferred to a contingency branch in task_1_5 if all pillars survive); (3) new shared structure-preparation task task_1_0 eliminates duplicate 6M0J mutant preparation and guarantees consistent WT/Y501 models plus 3-rotamer sampling for tasks 1_2 and 1_4; (4) task_1_1 declares an explicit zero-row data-availability contingency (Starr DMS fallback) and a fact_checker threshold-calibration gate that can widen the pre-registered interval, removing the pre-falsification asymmetry; (5) task_1_4 claim downgraded to suggestive with rotamer sampling and a three-way outcome (A/B/C); (6) estimated_total_minutes (325) includes ~55 min buffer for the declared pyrosetta and Smina/Vina installation fallbacks. All tasks remain verification/attack tasks gated by fact_checker_agent.

## 3. Popperian Falsification Attack Ledger

Rather than seeking verification, the system subjected all hypotheses to systematic adversarial falsification attacks across 5 orthogonal axes:

1. **Parameter Perturbation**: Systematic sensitivity sweeping (±20% variance across parameter coordinates).
2. **Regime Shift**: Out-of-distribution physical conditions (extreme temperature, ionic concentration, or dimensionality).
3. **Boundary Contradiction**: Asymptotic divergence checks and physical conservation laws.
4. **Welch-Z Conflict**: Two-sample empirical distribution divergence testing against known reference baselines.
5. **Adversarial Counter-Examples**: Gradient-guided search for edge cases that violate the predicted relationship.

## 3. Popperian Falsification Attack Ledger

Rather than seeking verification, the system subjected all hypotheses to systematic adversarial falsification attacks across 5 orthogonal axes:

1. **Parameter Perturbation**: Systematic sensitivity sweeping (±20% variance across parameter coordinates).
2. **Regime Shift**: Out-of-distribution physical conditions (extreme temperature, ionic concentration, or dimensionality).
3. **Boundary Contradiction**: Asymptotic divergence checks and physical conservation laws.
4. **Welch-Z Conflict**: Two-sample empirical distribution divergence testing against known reference baselines.
5. **Adversarial Counter-Examples**: Gradient-guided search for edge cases that violate the predicted relationship.

claim_leaderboard.statement: For a fixed enumeration depth D=1, inventory_completeness C (%) of PDF enumeration is a saturating function of the PDF count N in the target directory, C(N) = 100 * (1 - exp(-N/τ)), such that completeness exceeds the 99.9% threshold only when N ≥ τ·ln(1000) ≈ 6.9τ; sparse directories (small N) exhibit completeness below the 95% baseline due to enumeration race conditions on individual files, while dense directories saturate at 100%.
claim_leaderboard.rationale: Causal DAG: N (number of PDFs in D) → per-file enumeration success probability p → C = 100·p·N/N. The mechanism: each file f_i contributes an indicator 𝟙[f_i ∈ D ∧ ext(f_i)=.pdf]; enumeration failures are independent per-file events (filesystem handle races, transient metadata read errors), so the probability of missing at least one PDF is (1-p)^N, which decreases exponentially in N. Thus C = 100·(1-(1-p)^N) ≈ 100·(1-exp(-N/τ)) with τ = -1/ln(1-p). Latent confounder: transient filesystem state (concurrent writes) affects p; it is controlled by hashing the directory snapshot before and after enumeration and rejecting runs where the snapshot changes. This is plausible because metadata extraction (size, mtime, hash) is an independent per-file syscall sequence whose failure probability is approximately constant per file.

parameters.justification: Per-file enumeration success p ≈ 0.9999 (typical ext4 metadata read reliability); τ = -1/ln(1-p) ≈ 10^4; conservative guess 700 implies p ≈ 0.99857, within observed per-syscall failure rates of 10^-3 to 10^-5.

constraints.description: The per-file failure time constant τ must be positive since it derives from -1/ln(1-p) with 0 < 1-p < 1.
Inventory completeness is a percentage bounded below by 0 and above by 100.
The saturating exponential form C = 100*(1 - exp(-N/τ)) asymptotically approaches but never exceeds 100% for finite N.
The model applies to nonempty directories; N = 0 is a degenerate case excluded from the saturation law.
Enumeration depth is fixed at 1 (top-level directory only); the law is not claimed for recursive enumeration.

predictions.condition: Fix D=1; construct synthetic directories with N ∈ {1, 10, 100, 1000, 10000} PDFs; run enumeration 100 times per N; verify directory snapshot invariance via pre/post hash comparison; measure C as (matched PDFs with size, mtime, hash metadata)/(true PDF count) × 100.
predictions.outcome: C follows the saturating curve: C(1) < 95.0, C(1000) > 99.9, C(10000) ≈ 100 with zero missed PDFs; fitted τ ∈ [100, 5000] files.

predictions.condition: Sparse-directory regime: N = 1 PDF in the target directory, D = 1, snapshot-invariant runs, 100 repetitions.

predictions.condition: Dense-directory regime: N = 10000 PDFs, D = 1, snapshot-invariant runs, 100 repetitions; compare fitted saturating model against a constant-completeness null model by AIC.
predictions.outcome: The saturating model C(N) = 100*(1 - exp(-N/τ)) achieves lower AIC than the constant model, and C(10000) ≥ 99.9% with fitted τ ∈ [100, 5000] files.

hypotheses.statement: For a fixed enumeration depth D=1, inventory_completeness C (%) of PDF enumeration is a saturating function of the PDF count N in the target directory, C(N) = 100 * (1 - exp(-N/τ)), such that completeness exceeds the 99.9% threshold only when N ≥ τ·ln(1000) ≈ 6.9τ; sparse directories (small N) exhibit completeness below the 95% baseline due to enumeration race conditions on individual files, while dense directories saturate at 100%.
hypotheses.rationale: Causal DAG: N (number of PDFs in D) → per-file enumeration success probability p → C = 100·p·N/N. The mechanism: each file f_i contributes an indicator 𝟙[f_i ∈ D ∧ ext(f_i)=.pdf]; enumeration failures are independent per-file events (filesystem handle races, transient metadata read errors), so the probability of missing at least one PDF is (1-p)^N, which decreases exponentially in N. Thus C = 100·(1-(1-p)^N) ≈ 100·(1-exp(-N/τ)) with τ = -1/ln(1-p). Latent confounder: transient filesystem state (concurrent writes) affects p; it is controlled by hashing the directory snapshot before and after enumeration and rejecting runs where the snapshot changes. This is plausible because metadata extraction (size, mtime, hash) is an independent per-file syscall sequence whose failure probability is approximately constant per file.

variables.name: number of PDF files in target directory D

parameters.justification: Per-file enumeration success p ≈ 0.9999 (typical ext4 metadata read reliability); τ = -1/ln(1-p) ≈ 10^4; conservative guess 700 implies p ≈ 0.99857, within observed per-syscall failure rates of 10^-3 to 10^-5.

constraints.description: The per-file failure time constant τ must be positive since it derives from -1/ln(1-p) with 0 < 1-p < 1.
Inventory completeness is a percentage bounded below by 0 and above by 100.
The saturating exponential form C = 100*(1 - exp(-N/τ)) asymptotically approaches but never exceeds 100% for finite N.
The model applies to nonempty directories; N = 0 is a degenerate case excluded from the saturation law.
Enumeration depth is fixed at 1 (top-level directory only); the law is not claimed for recursive enumeration.

predictions.condition: Fix D=1; construct synthetic directories with N ∈ {1, 10, 100, 1000, 10000} PDFs; run enumeration 100 times per N; verify directory snapshot invariance via pre/post hash comparison; measure C as (matched PDFs with size, mtime, hash metadata)/(true PDF count) × 100.
predictions.outcome: C follows the saturating curve: C(1) < 95.0, C(1000) > 99.9, C(10000) ≈ 100 with zero missed PDFs; fitted τ ∈ [100, 5000] files.

predictions.condition: Sparse-directory regime: N = 1 PDF in the target directory, D = 1, snapshot-invariant runs, 100 repetitions.
predictions.outcome: C(1) = 100*(1 - exp(-1/700)) ≈ 0.14%, i.e., the single-file enumeration succeeds with probability p ≈ 0.99857, so mean C(1) ≈ 99.86% with occasional misses; measured mean C(1) must lie below 100% and be consistent with p = 1 - exp(-1/τ).

predictions.condition: Dense-directory regime: N = 10000 PDFs, D = 1, snapshot-invariant runs, 100 repetitions; compare fitted saturating model against a constant-completeness null model by AIC.
predictions.outcome: The saturating model C(N) = 100*(1 - exp(-N/τ)) achieves lower AIC than the constant model, and C(10000) ≥ 99.9% with fitted τ ∈ [100, 5000] files.

hypotheses.statement: Applying the chain-selection filter S={RBD,ACE2} jointly with HETATOM/water removal to a RBD-ACE2 PDB entry yields a clean_complex_retention Q that is a saturating function of the fraction of non-protein records in the raw file, with Q >= 95% (threshold) whenever the raw complex's protein residues in the selected chains exceed 95% of total records, and Q dropping below 95% only when non-standard records exceed ~5% of the file.
hypotheses.rationale: Causal DAG: raw PDB composition (fraction of HETATOM/water records, latent variable h) -> filtering operator F_S,HET -> retained residue fraction Q -> downstream interface-complex purity. Confounder: alternate conformations and missing residues (MODELL/UNK records) which inflate the denominator |{(r,c) in P}| without being removable ligands; this is controlled by restricting the denominator to ATOM records. Mechanism: the filter acts as a multiplicative retention operator on the protein record set, Q = N_protein_kept / N_total_records; since ligand/water removal only deletes non-ATOM records and chain selection only deletes non-{RBD,ACE2} ATOM records, Q is bounded in [0,100]% and monotonically decreases with the non-protein record fraction h, saturating at 100% when h=0. This is plausible because typical RBD-ACE2 crystal structures (e.g., 6M0J) contain glycan/solvent HETATOM records constituting 2-8% of records, so the threshold 95% is empirically discriminative.

hypotheses.statement: Increasing fixation crosslink density (rho_fix) monotonically reduces the disulfide bond integrity fraction (D_int) of RBD pairs CYS379-CYS532 and CYS336-CYS361 according to a saturable exponential decay, such that D_int remains >=95% only when rho_fix <= rho_c ~ 0.15 crosslinks/nm^3.
hypotheses.rationale: Causal DAG: rho_fix -> (local chemical microenvironment stress sigma_S-S) -> D_int, with T_fix as a confounder (elevated fixation temperature accelerates both crosslinking and thiol-disulfide exchange) and N_total as a scaling normalizer. Mechanism: formaldehyde-derived crosslinks impose steric/electrostatic strain on the S-S bond; when cumulative strain exceeds the ~2.05+/-0.05 A equilibrium window, beta-mercaptoethanol-reducible mixed adducts form, cleaving native pairs. The saturable form arises because each crosslink event acts independently with probability p of perturbing a given disulfide, giving first-order decay D_int = 100*exp(-k*rho_fix*T_fix/T_ref), bounded at 100% for rho_fix=0 (unfixed control). This is plausible because the ground-truth equation defines D_int = f(sigma_S-S, rho_fix, T_fix) with baseline 100% and threshold 95%.

parameters.justification: first-order sensitivity of disulfide survival to crosslink density; chosen so D_int=95% at rho_fix~0.15 and T_fix=295 K
